name: paper-legal
description: A cross-cutting legal-document drafting-CONVENTION taxonomy — ONE shared base + six per-category variant deltas (commercial-agreement / constitutional-agreement / schedule-exhibit / letter / preliminary-instrument / subscription-agreement). This is the reusable CONVENTION register (heading form, numbering scheme, cross-reference grammar) that governs how any paper-legal document should be drafted, distinct from the concrete per-document-type components (legal-agency-suite, legal-prospectus, legal-subscription-agreement) that already ship real CSS for specific document instances. Requested by project-documents; CSS/pt values are being delivered incrementally, Commercial first — most token bindings here are provisional placeholders until that lands.

variants.name: commercial-agreement
variants.description: Agency/underwriting/placement/engagement agreements. Flat 'N. Title.' bare-number, bold Title Case, left-aligned, NO 'ARTICLE'. Reference: initial reference-implementation pilot.

variants.name: constitutional-agreement
variants.description: Shareholder / Unanimous Shareholder / LP / Partnership agreements. Centered 'ARTICLE N' ALL-CAPS + 'N.N Title' sub-level, both case-distinct (HARD). Reference: the 3 Client A Shareholder Agreements.

variants.name: schedule-exhibit
variants.description: Schedules/Exhibits/Annexes attached to any of the above. 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered cover, internal headings inherit the parent document's scheme.

variants.name: letter
variants.description: Engagement/proposal letters. Numbered paragraph, bold Title-Case run-in if headed, never all caps.

variants.name: preliminary-instrument
variants.description: MOU / LOI / term sheet. MOU numbered/lettered A./B.; LOI letter-form; term sheet table/bullets.

variants.name: subscription-agreement
variants.description: Accredited-investor and Family & Friends securities subscription agreements — investor-completed fill-in forms with per-schedule named page counters, a two-tier typography system (serif body / sans fill-zones), and asymmetric binding-edge margins. Reference: an existing subscription-form CSS implementation covering accredited-investor and friends-and-family subscription documents. Tokens: {paper.semantic.legal-subscription-agreement.*} — renamed 2026-07-23 from the collision-prone 'legal-agreement' name.

aria: Clause numbering should use real <ol>/<li> (not visual-only numerals) so assistive technology can announce clause position, matching the precedent set by legal-agency-suite's body-clauses variant. Schedule/exhibit cover pages and signature blocks that use <table> purely for print layout, not to convey relational data, should carry role="presentation" — same precedent.
motion: Print-first static document family — no interaction states; renders to PDF (WeasyPrint per project-documents' existing pipeline).
open_questions: oq-1 (naming collision — RESOLVED 2026-07-23): closed by renaming the design-system-side token namespace (paper.semantic.legal-agreement.* -> paper.semantic.legal-subscription-agreement.*) rather than the project-documents-side CSS filename — operator's chosen direction, since nothing else depended on the old semantic-layer name and the primitive layer was already correctly named paper.primitive.type.legal-subscription.*. The subscription-agreement family also moved from a standalone component into this recipe's 6th variant in the same change. See DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE_legal-subscription-agreement-tokens.md.

oq-2 (overlap, flagged not silently duplicated): the schedule-exhibit variant covers the same ground as the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's schedule-cover variant (apage...epage named page counters). Recommend project-documents and the legal-agency-suite owner reconcile which component is authoritative for schedule/exhibit cover pages before both are built out further.

oq-3 (overlap, flagged not silently duplicated): the letter variant covers the same ground as legal-agency-suite's proposal-letter and mou-engagement-letter variants. Same reconciliation recommendation as oq-2.

oq-4 (capitalization house-style, per the source request's own §3.7): commercial-agreement's internal cross-reference capitalization is pending the operator's final pick between (a) capital 'Section' for ALL internal cross-references, or (b) the current split of capital whole-section vs. lowercase sub-tier. Component currently documents (a) as the DOMINANT recommendation per the source request; not yet operator-confirmed.

oq-5 (CSS delivery status): only commercial-agreement has a reference implementation in progress; constitutional-agreement has an existing, said-to-be-correct CSS file not yet reconciled into this vault's token layer; schedule-exhibit, letter, and preliminary-instrument have no CSS delivery scheduled yet beyond the taxonomy in this recipe.

oq-6 (BASE-vs-delta status, subscription-agreement variant): this variant's tokens are fully concrete (backed by a real, working CSS file) while paper-legal's own shared BASE remains provisional pending the reference implementation. Rather than block on BASE, this variant's fields are documented as their own concrete values under {paper.semantic.legal-subscription-agreement.*} — treat as a variant-level override of an undelivered BASE, not evidence that BASE itself is now finalized. Revisit once BASE lands to confirm which of this variant's fields genuinely turn out to be BASE-inheritable versus subscription-specific (the fill-zone tier-2 typography and per-schedule named counters are almost certainly subscription-specific; page margins and ink/placeholder-mark colors may turn out to be shared).
